neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Documents that the reusable contribution was not only a larger theorem range but a convexity method subsequently adapted to short intervals, uniformity in the moment parameter, derivative inequalities, Dirichlet L-functions, value distribution, and other L-function families.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Selberg Gaussian fluctuations independently predict k-squared growth
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Treats log|zeta| as approximately Gaussian and applies its exponential moment, converting variance proportional to log log T into the same T(log T)^(k^2) scale. This supplies a probabilistic representation of the exponent independent of the coefficient truncation.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The coefficient truncation isolates the prime-dependent factor a_k, while unitary characteristic-polynomial moments isolate g_k; hybrid prime-zero models explain why both factors are required in the same conjectural constant.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This is a synthesis of heuristics and conjectures, not a proof of zeta moment asymptotics, and the full polynomial statement cited is restricted to integer k.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A convergent coefficient mean value to the right of the critical line is pushed heuristically to the boundary by conductor-scale truncation; the diagonal coefficient sum then exposes both the k² logarithmic growth and an Euler product carrying prime arithmetic.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For σ>1 the shifted moment is asymptotic to T∑_{n≥1}d_k(n)^2/n^{2σ}. At σ=1/2 the series diverges, but truncating at n≤T gives a sum asymptotic to a_k(log T)^{k²}/Γ(k²+1), where a_k is an Euler product over primes. This predicts the T(log T)^{k²} moment scale.
directed.conceptual_reading: The coefficient diagonal converts an analytic mean value into multiplicative data. Its divergence rate supplies the universal-looking k² exponent, while Euler factorization isolates the arithmetic dependence prime by prime.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Generalized divisor coefficients d_k(n) and their truncated square sum are the bridge from ζ^k to a finite arithmetic model; the Euler product a_k compresses the prime contribution.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Replacing a divergent critical-line series by a truncation at T is heuristic, not a proof of the zeta moment asymptotic. This route predicts a_k and the scale but does not determine the additional g_k factor.
directed.uncertainty: The gamma normalization and Euler-product display are extraction-sensitive, though their roles and the k² exponent are explicit.

supported: The convergent shifted-moment coefficient sum, heuristic truncation at n≤T, emergence of the k² logarithmic exponent, and Euler product a_k are correctly identified.
